title: EXPLORE YOUR SERVICE IDEA WITH CHATGPT
content:
A service idea becomes useful when you can explain who it is for, what you would actually do, and whether delivering it fits your real capacity.

This interview is for a service you already have in mind. It should help you turn "I could do this" into a specific business direction before you spend time building packages, branding, or marketing.

WHAT YOU ARE TESTING
Does the service solve a recognizable task or problem? Do you have the ability to deliver it responsibly? Who would value it? Is the work one-time or recurring? Local or remote? Customized or standardized? How much direct time does each customer require?

The goal is not to prove demand. It is to define the service clearly enough that you know what would need to be tested next.

HOW TO USE THIS
Use the prompt below as an interview. If your idea is still vague, let ChatGPT help narrow it rather than filling in details you never chose.

COPY & PASTE INTO CHATGPT

During the interview:
- Ask one question at a time unless a small group of tightly related questions is genuinely easier to answer together.
- Use my answers before deciding what to ask next.
- If I say "I don't know," help me identify what I need to decide or research rather than inventing an answer.
- Explain unfamiliar business terms in plain language.
- Separate assumptions from facts requiring outside verification.
- Do not turn this into a marketing plan.

Interview me to explore this service idea: [DESCRIBE YOUR SERVICE IDEA].

Learn who I could serve, what task or problem I would handle, what skills and experience I bring, what I would actually do for the customer, whether the work should be local or remote, one-time or recurring, customized or standardized, and how much direct time delivery would require.

Ask about my schedule, desired workload, customer-contact preferences, tools or equipment, startup costs, and any parts of the work I do not want to perform.

Help me identify where the service may require licenses, insurance, certifications, contracts, data-security practices, professional rules, or other external requirements. Do not tell me I am compliant or qualified unless that has actually been verified.

Do not claim there is proven demand or invent market pricing.

At the end give me:
- Specific service direction
- Intended customer
- Task/problem being solved
- Core work I would perform
- One-time or recurring structure
- Local or remote delivery
- Approximate direct-work requirements based on my answers
- Major constraints and assumptions
- External facts or requirements to verify
- One concise business-direction statement

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Continue to PDF 44 to turn the direction into a clear offer.
